page0.text:
"We don't have much time. We'll beat Caster before Lancer and Archer settle their match."
"I know. We shouldn't waste our breath.
So, are you sure I can leave Caster to you, Tohsaka?"

page1.text:
"Yes. I'm sure I'll be thoroughly cornered, but don't help me. You can just try to keep Mr. Kuzuki away as long as possible."
We go past the chapel and head to the door leading to the courtyard.

page2.text:
I won't hesitate if Tohsaka says so.
...Most of all, I don't know if I could back Tohsaka up even if she were in trouble.
My opponent is Kuzuki. I wouldn't even be able to dodge his first attack if I'm paying attention to Tohsaka.

page3.text:
Caster's presence is getting closer.
She must not even be hiding her powers, as the church is surrounded by Caster's magical energy.
With this amount, she must already know about our raid.

page4.text:
"Trace, on."
I knit together the illusion as carefully as I can using the eight steps.
I got used to it, as his swords are in both hands within a minute.

page5.text:
"Ungh..."
I feel a light headache.
Even though I'm getting used to it, it takes some sort of toll on my body after all.
Projection is certainly affecting my body without me realizing it.

page6.text:
"..."
"Hm?"
Is it my imagination?
For a moment, I thought Tohsaka had hung her head in sorrow while running next to me.

page7.text:
We go down through the darkness.
We run down the stairs that go underground and go out to the open area.
And after that, we jump off of the railing of the stairs down to the sanctuary like before.

page8.text:
"Oh. You guys are like monkeys, jumping down like that.
I don't know why you're in such a hurry, but at least use the stairs if you're human."

page9.text:
We land in the sanctuary.
This is supposed to be a surprise attack, but Caster greets us with composure.

page10.text:
...
There is Souichirou Kuzuki standing beside Caster.
...I feel no enmity or bloodlust from him.
That is his battle posture. His clear murderous intent is even hiding the dreadfulness of that man.
In that regard, he's even more like an assassin than the Servant Assassin right now.

page11.text:
Saber is at the altar.
The situation is the same as two days ago.
Saber is still tied from the ceiling with her head hanging down.

page12.text:
...
I'm relieved we made it, but at the same time, it worries me how awfully quiet she is.
I feel like Saber was a bit more in pain before.
She was shaking slightly, as if breathing with her whole body to go against Caster's magical energy.
But she's silent now like she's frozen.

page13.text:
"..."
I have a bad feeling.
It's good Assassin is not here, but we won't be able to get out of here alive if my worries are true...

page14.text:
"We're here, Caster. I thought things through, but I've decided to have you eliminated.
You're an eyesore, you're in my way, you're troublesome, and I don't like the way you dress. You look like you came from the countryside with that purple robe in this day and age."

page15.text:
Tohsaka insults Caster, who is full of composure, as if refusing to lose against her.
Even though she's saying such things, she must actually be feeling the opposite from the way she's slowly closing in on her.

page16.text:
...
...Now's not the time for me to be concerned about Saber either.
If Tohsaka is going to close in on Caster counterclockwise, I'll close in clockwise.
Caster and Kuzuki. If we're going to separate them, we have to attack them from both sides and isolate our enemies.

page17.text:
"...Heh. You seem to be making a big misunderstanding as someone who was let go. Are all mages nowadays so reckless? No wonder Archer gave up on you."
Tohsaka's insults must've worked on her, as Caster is glaring only at Tohsaka.

page18.text:
I use that opening to move.
I move to the other side of Tohsaka, where I can attack Caster from the other side.
...
Kuzuki watches that in silence.

page19.text:
...I knew it.
There's no way that man won't notice something like this.
He's aware of everything.
The fact that we're trying to defeat them one by one, and the fact that Tohsaka has some kind of plan.

page20.text:
Even with that in mind, Kuzuki is letting Caster do as she wishes.
...It's not like Kuzuki is being manipulated by Caster.
He became Caster's Master of his own free will.
But, still... Based on his passivity, Kuzuki is close to a puppet.

page21.text:
A Servant who is skilled in providing backup using magecraft,
and a Master who is skilled in hand-to-hand combat.
Their roles are reversed, and I feel like their way of being is reversed as well.
Caster who persistently seeks the Holy Grail, and the Master protects Caster without his own will.

page22.text:
...
That makes me think without a reason.
That if Caster was a Master and Kuzuki was just a Servant who protected her, then they wouldn't have fallen so low.

page23.text:
...
Tohsaka looks over at me.
It means our positions are perfect.
Then... The match will be settled if either of us attacks.
Whether Tohsaka and I get defeated or Tohsaka defeats Caster before that, our battle with Caster will end here.

page24.text:
"Let us start then. This is the third time I'm fighting you. I'll settle this for the last time."
Tohsaka steps in closer to Caster.

page25.text:
"You're talking big. I doubt it, but do you seriously think you can win against me, young lady?
In that case, we don't even need to fight. I shall let you go again this time, so that you can go fix that personality of yours."

page26.text:
"Of course I can win.
Isn't that right? There's no way a first-class mage can lose to a third-class mage like you."

page27.text:
"..Is that so? Then I suppose it can't be helped.
It seems that I need to discipline that arrogant mouth of yours, young lady."

page28.text:
They brace themselves at the same time.
With a few meters between them, they look like mirror images.

page29.text:
That is the signal.
I attack the defenseless Caster...
"...!"
And of course, I'm blocked by Kuzuki's blow.

page30.text:
...The ghost-like assassin is in front of me.
I don't have the composure to watch over Tohsaka and Caster's fight.
He already knows my intentions.
He will not let me buy time.
Letting out the snake that cornered even Saber, Souichirou Kuzuki comes to take my life.

page31.text:
I can hold him off for one minute at most.
That should be the same for Tohsaka.
Originally, this was a battle with no chance of victory had the roles not been reversed.
There is no way we could win against enemies who surpass us in both hand-to-hand combat and magecraft.

page32.text:
But looking at it the other way, we can at least put up a fight.
Tohsaka would be killed in an instant if she fought Kuzuki,
and Caster would end me just by pointing at me if I fought her.
On the other hand, we might not be able to win, but at least we won't get killed in an instant.

page33.text:
...In other words...
This battle is not about how we can defeat them, but...
A battle like walking on a tightrope to see how long we can hold off an opponent who is superior to us.
